sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The company builds industrial civil structures for cement, power and dairy plants, including complex/high-rise structures, and is moving into steel, logistics parks and integrated civil, structural, mechanical and electrical work. Revenue is generated through project execution and certification under percentage-of-completion accounting, not simply through orders being announced. Customers can provide advances; the contractor provides guarantees, employs labour, buys materials and equipment, and waits for certification, retention and final settlement. Work descriptions, long operating history and owned machinery establish real execution substance. Management reports 270+ equipment units, approximately 1,400 staff/8,000 workforce and operations across 13 states; these are management descriptions, not audited sustainable capacity measures.

Contract durations are commonly about 12 months for cement and 18–24 months for power/dairy, but site readiness and monsoons can move revenue between halves. Equipment utilization, mobilization, customer acceptance and cash release are therefore as important as nominal backlog. No separate recurring annuity business is established. Working-capital advances are financing tied to delivery obligations, not distributable free money; retention remains an operating receivable. The shift toward end-to-end execution can enlarge wallet share but also exposes the company to disciplines and coordination risk beyond historical civil expertise. [S1][S2][S4][S9]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
The plausible moat is a narrow qualification-and-execution advantage: completed industrial references, owned equipment, experienced project teams and repeat relationships lower coordination risk for a customer building a complex plant. These can win repeat work without demonstrating monopoly pricing. A competing contractor still needs people, equipment, working capital, guarantees and an acceptable record, but no evidence supports a quantified decade-long replication barrier. Tendering, concentrated customers and incomplete escalation protection limit bargaining power. Management's earlier 10% market-share claim lacks an independently verified addressable-market denominator and is not scored as fact.

Primary economic comparators discipline the thesis. Ahluwalia's April 2026 CARE rationale shows AA−/Stable/A1+, FY25 revenue ₹4,093 crore and 8.21%PBILDT margin, with 9MFY26 growth 12%, margin 11%, substantial liquidity and a ₹18,057 crore order book. Yet collections lengthened and private/NCR project concentration remained. Vascon's August 2026 CRISIL downgrade toBBB+/Stable/A2 followedFY26 revenue ₹949 crore, down 12%, margin 5.7%, weakerQ1FY27 and increasing debt; its real-estate/EPC mix is not directly comparable. SPML's June rationale describesFY26 revenue about ₹838 crore and very long 400–500-day gross-current-asset cycle, legacy restructuring and a mixed ₹5,000 crore order book. These are operating and financing benchmarks, not automatic valuation multiples or rankings. Goel's historical operating cash is encouraging relative to stressed peers, but customer advances explain part of that advantage. [S1][P1][P2][P3]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Standalone revenueFY21–26 was ₹159.2109,205.7627,270.7321,386.0599,589.9845 and 657.2965 crore. Annual additions were ₹46.5518,64.9694,115.3278,203.9246 and 67.3120 crore. The preselected five-year CAGR is 32.79%; three-year cross-check 34.40%, four-year 33.69%; ten-yearND. The six-year table preserves originalFY21/22, restatedFY23–25 and statutoryFY26 bases rather than claiming identical restatement coverage. FY21 pandemic conditions flatter the starting point; no acquisition contribution was identified, but exact volume/pricing/mix allocation isND.

Growth slowed from 52.82% inFY25 to 11.41% inFY26. H1FY26 revenue ₹245.3770 crore fell 9.84% versus ₹272.1642 crore; derivedH2₹411.9195 crore rose 29.61% versus ₹317.8203 crore. Management attributed the weak first half to prolonged/heavy monsoon. This is a project-timing recovery, not proof of smooth quarterly compounding. Latest verified financial year isFY26; no H1FY27 statutory revenue was recovered by cutoff, and theOctober update is not used to manufactureTTM.

FY25 top customer 42.69%, top 5 84.07% and top 10 95.69% refer to construction revenue, not a diversified customer franchise. Sector mix was 74.40% cement,19.73% power and 5.87% dairy; FY26 management mix moves to 84/14/2. Strong historic growth therefore coexists with elevated concentration and dependence on client capital-spending cycles. [S1][S2][S3][S4][S8]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Order book grew from ₹438.49 crore at March 2025 to ₹1,291.23 crore atMarch 2026, roughly 1.96 timesFY26 revenue. September's issuer update says about ₹1,300+crore, with healthy execution, satisfactory new booking and an expected pickup in closures as geopolitical/macro conditions stabilize. The update also cites entry into logistics parks and steel and exploration of data centres/power. These are management statements, not audited margin, collection or bank-capacity forecasts. Exact opening backlog+intake−execution−cancellations reconciliation and customer-funded margin waterfall areND.

Base assumptions grow sales 15/15/12/10/10/8%, with 10% EBITDA after recurring LC and other bank fees, gross operating working capital 20% ofsales and customer advances 15→14%; capex 4.5→4% includes the committed ₹13.9925 crore once. Bull 25/22/20/18/15/12% growth,10.5→11% margin and stronger advance support require substantially better delivery. These cases are not commitments. Capital intensity includes equipment, reusable shuttering stock, retention, operating deposits and guarantees, not just plant balance. Management's high coreROCE denominator excludes financial assets and is not incremental post-taxROIC. The detailed balance-sheet bridge yields attractive proxies but cannot attribute profit to specific reinvested capital, soCAP andGQS remainNS. TAM and an attractive order book do not override this evidence gap. [S1][S2][S4][S9]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Promoter-family ownership 71.83% provides continuity and control; theSeptember declaration reports no promoter pledge, non-disposal undertaking or other encumbrance, and no outstanding warrants, convertibles orESOPs. The 5,817,060 locked-in shares are not pledged shares. Current issued shares independently match the official master. FY26 audit andCARO are unmodified, with no reported fraud or going-concern uncertainty; no evidence was found of an FY26 auditor resignation. These are meaningful positives, not a guarantee of minority alignment.

Related-party revenue toAnuj ₹8.4061 crore, purchases fromGoelHisar ₹6.4096 crore and a property sale toGanpati ₹3.8 crore deserve continuing commercial-term scrutiny. Director remuneration totals ₹1.38 crore, with separately disclosed relatives' employment costs. A prior relatedDurvaLLP guarantee ₹25 crore and partnership exposure were disclosed historically; exit on 30 November 2024 andFY25 withdrawal ₹8.4032 crore are positive developments, but a documentary guarantee-release check is still appropriate. Do not automatically carry ₹25 crore as a current extra debt claim or quietly assume proof of release. Unquoted investment ₹1.73 crore inGreenWings within ₹1.79 crore total nonquoted holdings is noncore, excluded from free cash.

Execution evidence is generally favorable: FY26 revenue grew 11.41%, above theMarch rating's 8–10% expectation, and IPO equipment/debt objects were substantially used. Conversely,H1 weakness and new disciplines argue against extrapolating flawless delivery. AGM authority up to ₹1,200 crore for borrowing/security is not a bank sanction or warrant allotment; Septemberboard outcome concernedKPIs/CSR trust. Kuber and labour disputes remain allegations/contested claims; company responses and limited subsequent procedural evidence are preserved in the bear case and source register. [S1][S2][S5][S6][S10][S11]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
FY23–26 cumulative CFO of ₹173.7084 crore versus PAT of ₹121.5222 crore gives 1.4294 times conversion. Subtracting all finance costs, since interest is classified in financing, gives 1.2772 times. Cash capex is not used to excuse CFO: cumulative FCF before finance costs remains ₹76.6809 crore. FY26 CFO of ₹62.8247 crore less ₹35.1857 crore capex and ₹10.1973 crore finance costs leaves ₹17.4417 crore. However, customer advances rose ₹74.7779 crore to ₹116.6376 crore. Removing only that increase gives negative ₹11.9532 crore as a sensitivity, not corrected audited CFO. Advances finance future work and can reverse.

Receivables rose 153.15% to ₹70.294 crore and inventory 234.64% to ₹37.3298 crore against 11.41% revenue growth. Good receivables are ₹63.1539 crore not yet due and ₹7.1401 crore under six months; old doubtful balances of ₹0.9273 crore are fully provided. Retention of ₹49.8395 crore adds another collection layer. Shuttering/material inventory of ₹23.7007 crore versus ₹1.612 crore creates reusable-equipment expense and capital-timing uncertainty. Capex, inventory and depreciation must be assessed together.

Normalize FY26 operating EBITDA of ₹73.2723 crore by charging recurring LC discount costs of ₹6.5817 crore to operations, giving ₹66.6906 crore or 10.146% margin. Remaining finance costs of ₹3.6156 crore include interest and other bank fees. Forecast EBITDA margins also absorb recurring noninterest bank fees, with debt interest modeled separately. Removing all other income of ₹7.9818 crore is a conservative core-earnings sensitivity, not a claim that every rupee is exceptional. Weighted EPS of ₹35.25 uses 13,122,885 average shares; current 14,449,600 claims give ₹32.0136, below FY25 pre-IPO EPS of ₹33.7192. The 10:1 bonus was not economic dilution; 3,084,400 fresh shares were.

Operating invested capital of ₹120.5916→143.4001 crore reconciles to the independently classified financing identity within ₹0.001 crore. ROIC of 32.79%, one-year incremental return of 24.29% and ROCE of 43.72% are book proxies, not attributable incremental economics. FY23/24 gratuity restatements are preserved. FY25 restated CFO of ₹38.4372 crore versus the statutory comparator of ₹38.3351 crore differs by ₹0.1021 crore, substantially explained by classification, tax and rounding. FY22 bank-inclusive cash of ₹13.4788 crore versus FY23 opening cash equivalents of ₹8.2584 crore is a ₹5.2204 crore perimeter gap, not inferred cash destruction. Prepaid expenses of ₹0.1738 crore stay in working capital; tax assets of ₹2.9105 crore are not cash; operating property is not added atop enterprise value. [S1][S2][S3]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹400, market capitalization of ₹577.984 crore is 12.49 times FY26 PAT, 14.35 times PAT after removing all other income at 25% tax, and 2.27 times book. Cash-only EV adds debt of ₹7.973 crore and deducts unrestricted cash of ₹19.3422 crore, giving ₹566.6148 crore or 8.50 times adjusted EBITDA. A maximum-liquidity sensitivity gives EV of ₹483.1746 crore, but is not the baseline because additional FD encumbrance is unverified. Headline cash/investments of ₹145.1042 crore include pledged FDs of ₹26.5077 crore, restricted IPO money of ₹14.0241 crore and unquoted holdings of ₹1.79 crore. Baseline March opening cash of ₹19.3422 crore plus quoted funds at market value of ₹24.0355 crore, less 1% realization cost, gives ₹43.137345 crore. The unused IPO allocation funds committed capex once, not new forecast equity. OFS proceeds of ₹19.0307 crore belong to sellers. GST-inclusive IPO expenses differ by ₹0.9320 crore from the cash/equity expense bridge, never treated as extra money.

The cash model first bridges March 2026 to the October 2026 entry date using expressly assumed uniform intra-year operating, investing and financing accrual. This is unverified pro-forma opening wealth, not actual H1 results or earnings credited to the investor. A separate investor ledger starts on 19 October 2026 with that assumed October cash/debt/WC balance, includes only the remaining FY27 flows, then FY28–31 and a final 202/366 FY32 stub through 19 October 2031. The return horizon is exactly five years; no pre-entry distribution is counted. Full FY32 revenue is an interpolation aid, not post-horizon cash assumed earned. No incremental borrowing is modeled, but existing OD continuation to FY30 is assumed and unverified. The all-debt-repaid-in-FY27 sensitivity removes that continuation. Term debt is otherwise amortized over FY27–29.

The operating cash floor is 2% of revenue run rate in every period and remains inside the business at terminal. Terminal EV/EBITDA multiples are 5/8/11 in bear/base/bull. Ending debt, excess cash, one-time legacy DTL of ₹1.6832 crore, gratuity payment of ₹3.6065 crore and rescue claims are explicit. Pledged operating deposits, property, prepaid expenses, tax assets and unverified FDs are never double-added. Base conditional IRR is 14.30%, with a conditional 15% hurdle entry of ₹387.90; bull is 32.09%. These are not ordinary investment returns or supported purchase ranges.

The bear has its first annual cash gap in FY27 and a peak gap of ₹25.8605 crore; its interpolated October entry bridge also falls slightly below the cash floor. All non-rescue returns and entries are null despite later cash recovery. A separate hypothetical rescue immediately after entry raises ₹26.66034 crore at ₹200 per share with 3% fees, adding 1,333,017 shares. That is 9.23% share-count expansion and 8.45% ownership dilution, producing negative 14.18% rescue IRR. Reverse expectations cross the 15% hurdle near 12.8% flat growth only under the specified margin, working-capital and exit conditions. Growth/multiple, advances/gross-WC, claims, FD release, execution costs and 12/15/18% hurdles are embedded. Ordinary IRRs and entry prices remain null throughout. [S2][S5][M1][Q1]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest bear case combines reversal of advance funding, weaker collections and lower margins, rather than assuming construction demand disappears. A large cement customer delays work; advances reduce toward 7–10% of sales while gross working capital rises toward 26%; subcontractor/material costs and integrated-execution problems compress margins. The linked bear starts with a 20% sales decline and 6.5% margin, followed by gradual recovery. It breaches the cash floor in FY27. A peak ₹25.8605 crore funding need cannot be treated as an automatic loan. Financial assets and low audited debt are counterevidence, but unverified FD liens or guarantee calls can remove protection. A 10% call on ₹128.1414 crore guarantees equals ₹12.81414 crore. This is a separate stress, not an asserted payable or automatically additive to customer-advance obligations.

Legal risk is qualified. Kuber Alloys claims ₹0.7686896 crore plus interest; the company disputed quantum while acknowledging a lower unpaid amount in its defence. The claimant's application for judgment on admission was dismissed on 27 September 2023 and appealed. A May 2026 mirror order only adjourned proceedings, not a merits resolution. A ₹0.5527 crore labour award was appealed; the issuer says it was denied adequate hearing, cross-examination and consideration of material evidence. An August 2025 High Court mirror order directed expedited appeal disposal without deciding merits. Procedural dates differ between the issuer summary and mirror; they are not silently harmonized, and later status is unverified. GST contingencies total ₹0.0514 crore. These do not establish fraud, nor does company disagreement erase them. Claim sensitivities separate Kuber/GST/labour and guarantee shocks instead of stacking every disclosure as certain loss.

Permanent-loss risk is material: bad debt, execution losses, guarantee claims and rescue equity can permanently impair per-share value. The primary thesis-break variable is advance-adjusted operating cash and verified usable funding through the work cycle. Sustained negative cash while advances fall and guarantees/retention grow would defeat the self-funded growth thesis. Positive cumulative CFO and the unmodified audit are important contrary evidence, not a blanket clearance. [S1][S2][C1][C2]

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
Fivefold price appreciation in five years requires 37.97% annual compounding; tenfold requires 58.49%. With unchanged shares, a 15 times terminal P/E and 7% net margin, 5× requires revenue of about ₹2,752.30 crore and 10× about ₹5,504.61 crore, compared with ₹657.30 crore currently. This is algebra, not a price forecast. Such scale must be financed through equipment, staff, guarantees, mobilization, retention and project risk. The current order book of about ₹1,300 crore cannot itself validate either outcome: execution reduces backlog, which must be replenished by new orders.

A 5× outcome could be economically possible for a much larger, more diversified contractor with sustained margins and limited dilution, but it is demanding. Available capacity, customer and attributable project-return evidence is insufficient to support a 10× thesis. Classification: possible but demanding for 5×; speculative/unsupported for 10×. Lower exit multiples or rescue/warrant dilution raise required earnings further. No probability or sensational target is assigned. The realistic first milestones are verified post-IPO per-share growth, durable collections and incremental returns, not extrapolating pandemic-base CAGR into an assured multibagger. [S1][S2][M1][Q1]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
1. Obtain current bank/FD-lien and guarantee schedules. Baselines are audited debt ₹7.973 crore, known pledged FDs ₹26.5077 crore and ambiguous FDs ₹59.2378 crore. Dated sanctions are required; AGM permission and the March rating do not suffice.
2. Track customer advances of ₹116.6376 crore against executed work and cash. Rapid withdrawal while gross working capital remains high is a warning; verified funding insufficiency is a thesis break.
3. Track receivables of ₹70.294 crore and retention of ₹49.8395 crore against invoices, certification and collection. Ageing beyond one year or new unprovided disputes are warnings.
4. Reconcile reusable shuttering inventory of ₹23.7007 crore, equipment capex and depreciation. A lower capex ratio alone does not demonstrate improved capital economics.
5. Obtain a backlog roll-forward from ₹1,291.23 crore in March and ₹1,300+ crore in September, including customer, margin, advance and deadline exposure.
6. Compare H1FY27 with the ₹245.377 crore H1FY26 base only when statutory results are published; never double a seasonal half-year to manufacture TTM.
7. Verify remaining IPO funds of ₹14.0241 crore and committed capex of ₹13.9925 crore settle once. Obtain the GST/timing explanation for the ₹0.9320 crore expense bridge.
8. Require project/cohort incremental-return evidence before scoring CAP. Average core ROCE is not enough.
9. Track full-share EPS of ₹32.01 against reported ₹35.25 and any new equity. No warrants were declared in September, but future authority does not mean zero dilution risk.
10. Monitor related-party terms, historical LLP guarantee release and court outcomes, retaining both allegations and company responses.
11. Before implementation, refresh the 400-share lot, current series, missing 28 July observation, exchange turnover and bid-ask depth. The recent 20-day, 5%-participation whole-lot exit estimate of 15 sessions is illustrative, not assured.

This is a research monitoring plan, not a scheduled automation, trade or request for external contact. [S1][S2][S5][S9][S10][M1][Q1]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Hold — unresolved. Goel has a stronger historical operating/cash record than a typical unproven SME listing, but evidence does not yet support calling it a high-quality compounder or ranking it on complete BQS/GQS/IAS points. G1 and G2 are Clear on reviewed evidence, not guarantees. G3 Hold reflects current verification, not reported default; G4 Conditional reflects implementation uncertainty, not evidenced suspension. No hard governance or funding-failure override is applied. The practical research priority is current liquidity/funding and attributable capital returns, followed by sustainable per-share growth.

A potential new buyer should not treat the ₹387.90 conditional hurdle entry as an approved entry price: it depends on a hypothetical cash-balanced operating path and unverified October opening/current funding. An existing holder would review advance funding, client concentration, real cash and lot constraints before focusing on headline P/E. No holding, cost basis or portfolio allocation is known. Three lots cost ₹480,000, not exactly ₹500,000; four cost ₹640,000. Recent whole-lot trading could make staged implementation much slower than continuous rupee-turnover estimates suggest. A lower price cannot fix poor cash or missing bank proof. Conversely, resolved funding evidence and demonstrated incremental returns could improve the classification without requiring a new business story. [S1][S2][M1][Q1]

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary issuer prospectus, original FY22 accounts, FY26 annual report/results, IPO monitoring, ownership and business updates anchor historical facts. CRISIL provides dated credit context; comparable rating-agency files benchmark economics, not valuation assurance. The official interoperable master verifies issued shares, lot and eligibility. Secondary BSE OHLCV gives dated quotes/volumes and proxy turnover only. Direct BSE and court downloads returned 403. An issuer-filing mirror was used for the October business update, while court text remains limited third-party evidence. The September ownership file is issuer-linked but named Report-draft; its exact historical upload timestamp was not independently established. Only aggregate ownership facts are retained. No raw issuer PDF, OCR, image, personal identifier or shareholders' personal data is placed in private Library backups.

Open questions are dated usable cash, FD encumbrance and bank headroom; project incremental-return attribution; price/volume and customer/backlog bridges; advance runoff and retention recovery; shuttering classification; exact IPO GST/timing; historical related guarantee release and latest dispute status; and complete 60-session turnover, depth and restrictions. Forecast growth, margins, working capital, deposits, capex, debt amortization, legacy claims, terminal multiples, cash floor and rescue fee/price are analyst assumptions. The March-to-October bridge is an unverified pro-forma starting balance, not claimed current financial results. Every ordinary return and entry remains null; unfunded conditional cells also remain null.

Safe extracts, code and results reproduce the analytical artifact in isolation, but fresh source authentication requires original URLs and hash comparison. No trades or third-party communications were performed as part of this research. [S1][S2][S3][S5][S6][M1][Q1]

valuation.source_verification: Model relies on sanitized primary-source financial extracts. Original PDFs and hashes retained only locally; source-free restoration requires fresh original downloads for source authentication.

liquidity.quote_type: Secondary historical BSE close, not executable live offer
liquidity.restrictions: 19 Oct official interoperable master: eligible SM row, normal-market status 6; ST ineligible. Normal SME series; direct BSE reason/surveillance category and live bid-ask unverified. No live bid or offer inspected.
limitations: Missing BSE source records are unknown, never filled as observed zero.
NSE archives provide calendar only. BSE issuer not in NSE bhavcopy is not zero trading.
Value equals close times volume only as proxy; low/high times volume bound actual value.
Historical capacity does not promise a future fill, especially in 400-share lots.
